A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a nucleus can be considered as a rotating rigid body if the deviations from a spherical shape are sufficiently small.
the angular velocity is a constant for the upper phase of a rotational band.
the angular velocity of the nucleus immediately after back-bending is a unique function of the angular momentum, independent of its value and of the shape of the nucleus.

the moment of inertia of a nucleus is a function of the angular momentum.
